papers.summary: A post-step spectral weight-decay update lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss. The paper also reports clean-test gains under label noise.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses training for low-rank compressibility, spectral regularization, and memorization.

evidence.quote: spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
Regularization coefficients are calibrated in separate tuning runs using final clean-validation accuracy

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting low-rank gradient subspaces during LLM pretraining. At rank 32 on the reported 1B LLaMA task, its validation perplexity is 29.14 versus 33.82 for GaLore, with lower measured optimizer-step peak memory.
papers.relevance: A direct quality–memory comparison for low-rank gradient optimization.

evidence.quote: at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Monarch-Muon applies matrix-aware updates to structured factors. Fixed-structure quality runs favor it over Monarch-AdamW, while separate systems measurements examine memory and step time at larger reference widths.
papers.relevance: Connects parameterization and optimizer geometry to pretraining quality, memory, and throughput.

evidence.quote: Monarch–Muon achieves lower final validation loss than Monarch–AdamW in all four structured comparisons
The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: ORCA applies soft orthogonality regularization early in LLM training, then removes it. Reported runs show lower final validation loss than Muon with small measured overhead in an 8B MoE setup.
papers.relevance: Tests how the timing of spectral regularization affects effective rank and training quality, though not low-rank compressibility.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA, Qwen3, and fine-grained mixture-of-experts models ranging from 130M to 8B parameters, ORCA achieves lower final validation loss than Muon.
Peak memory is 101.41 ​ GB 101.41\,\mathrm{GB} and 101.66 ​ GB 101.66\,\mathrm{GB} , respectively.

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon’s geometry to favor structured MLP-channel pruning. In a 1B language-model experiment, it retains perplexity near its own unpruned result through 80% pruning, but starts from worse unpruned perplexity than Muon.
papers.relevance: Directly tests whether an optimizer can make a trained model more compressible, while exposing the quality tradeoff.

evidence.quote: On the unpruned models, Muon achieves lower perplexity ( 10.92 10.92 versus 12.84 12.84 for BMuon), but its performance degrades rapidly under pruning.
BMuon preserves its unpruned performance up to 80 % 80\% pruning, reaching 12.86 12.86 with activation ranking and 12.85 12.85 with μ \mu ranking.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Proposes a Riemannian metric and induced preconditioning for the redundant two-factor LoRA parameterization. The paper reports language and vision experiments, with retrieved timing evidence from CLIP image classification.
papers.relevance: A direct match for LoRA factorization geometry and optimization.

evidence.quote: This relation induces a quotient manifold where matrices $(BG^{-1}, AG^\top)$ for all $G$ are identified, eliminating redundant directions along which the loss value remains unchanged.
we proposed a Riemannian metric that is specifically tailored to LoRA to close the gap to full fine-tuning at the weight level.

papers.title: A Riemannian Geometry for Low-rank Adaptation

papers.summary: DT-LoRA periodically captures principal residual-gradient directions outside the current LoRA tangent space within a fixed rank budget. It reports language-task comparisons, while the retrieved step-time measurement is from a vision setup.
papers.relevance: Addresses inaccessible directions in factorized LoRA and practical adaptation under a rank constraint.

evidence.quote: eight commonsense reasoning tasks using LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B; and GLUE using DeBERTaV3-base. Under matched trainable parameter budgets, DT-LoRA consistently outperforms LoRA and its variants.
Time is the steady-state per-iteration training time with τ = 5 \tau=5 , measured on one A100 for OVDG-SS

papers.title: DT-LoRA: Reaching Beyond the Tangent Space of Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Defines LoRA adapter compressibility by serialized size needed to retain held-out fine-tuning gain. It finds that the measured rate depends on the frozen base model, not just the dataset or weight-reconstruction error.
papers.relevance: Challenges simple rank- or reconstruction-based measures of useful low-rank fine-tuning compression.

evidence.quote: the same datasets can require substantially different rates across frozen models, with their ordering changing across receivers.
R ⋆ R^{\star} is an operational, codec-dependent rate rather than an information-theoretic optimum

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: CORE is a training-free research-agent harness that retrieves broad passages but supplies concise snippets, with source expansion and deduplication. Controlled closed-search comparisons report higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than two harness baselines.
papers.relevance: A close reference for retrieval and context management in the planned digest agent.

evidence.quote: CORE retrieves whole passages to judge relevance, then reuses the reranker’s token-level similarities to return only the most relevant snippet from each one.
Across three agent models and three benchmarks, CORE achieves higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

papers.summary: Idea2Prior records discovery, candidate identity, filtering, and evidence for auditable idea-to-paper ranking. Its historical Hit@5 comparison favors it overall, but not on HARD queries, and is not a matched general-research or cost comparison.
papers.relevance: Directly informs candidate screening and evidence tracking for the digest agent.

evidence.quote: it preserves search queries, candidate identities, assessments, filtering reasons, PDF availability, and the final ranking.
they do not establish general Deep Research superiority, calibrated novelty assessment, or a matched baseline cost advantage.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: The digest is selected from the fixed eligible corpus; unexamined papers may be stronger matches.
Some retrieved HTML passages have imperfect table and equation formatting. Numerical claims should be checked against the original tables before reuse.
Ori’s quoted memory measure is optimizer-step peak memory, not total peak training memory. Monarch-Muon’s larger-scale systems measurements are separate from its complete quality runs.
BMuon’s reported 1B compressibility gain is for structured MLP-channel pruning, not SVD low-rank compression, and comes with worse unpruned perplexity than Muon.
